verdicts.title: Recent advances on the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The log-rank conjecture is one of the fundamental open problems in communication complexity. It speculates that the deterministic communication complexity of any two-party function is equal to the log of the rank of its associated matrix, up to polynomial factors. Despite much research, we still know very little about this conjecture. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract surveys the log-rank conjecture relating communication complexity to matrix rank, but makes no mention of quasi-group representations or 'minimal order of representations' (mqr), so it shares the communication-complexity/rank framework without addressing the specific quasi-group claim.

verdicts.title: Applications of Monotone Rank to Complexity Theory
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Raz's recent result \cite{Raz2010} has rekindled people's interest in the study of \emph{tensor rank}, the generalization of matrix rank to high dimensions, by showing its connections to arithmetic formulas. In this paper, we follow Raz's work and show that \emph{monotone rank}, the monotone variant of tensor rank and matrix rank, has applications in algebraic complexity, quantum computing and communication complexity.
